# MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3 Calibration checks - Machining heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Scope
This document describes calibration verification checks required for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02). It covers the critical checks that influence quench timing, sensor response, and lubrication interface function for production runs. The intent is to provide clear procedural steps, background rationale, and recordkeeping expectations so that technicians performing maintenance can demonstrate the furnace meets operational readiness before release to process.

Background and rationale
EQ-P2-L3-HT02 has controls and actuators that directly affect the quenching sequence and the mechanical handling interfaces. Variability in quench initiation and in actuator response can lead to nonconforming metallurgy or increased mechanical wear. Calibration verification focuses on sensing elements, timing outputs, and the lubrication interface. The quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds. Compliance to this value is critical to maintain process repeatability. Use lubricant specified by the maintenance parts list for bearing locations and moving slides; the lubricant part number for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is CFW-LUB-373.

Tools
- Standard instrumentation used for signal verification and functional check of furnace controls as specified in SOP-P2-L3-05.  
- Calibration reference for timing verification and signal capture as required by SB-1023.  
- Approved lubricant container labeled with CFW-LUB-373.  
- Hand tools and protective equipment as required by plant safety protocols found in SB-1039.

Procedure
Preparation
- Verify work authorization and lockout/tagout in accordance with plant maintenance rules. Confirm SOP-P2-L3-05 for any safety-specific preparatory steps. Ensure the area around EQ-P2-L3-HT02 is clean and free of process material so instrumentation can be mounted and read without obstruction.

Functional baseline
- With controls in service mode, initiate the furnace through a controlled functional cycle that exercises the quench initiation pathway and the handling actuators. Capture the timing sequence with the timing capture device and with control panel status indicators. The focus is on the time between the final heat profile hold release signal and the quench valve actuation. Compare captured timing to the quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds.

Sensor verification
- Visually inspect sensors for physical damage, secure mounting, and clean sensing surfaces. Verify electrical and signal connections are secure. For any sensor that exhibits intermittent or noisy output during the functional baseline, remove for bench testing and compare against the sensor manufacturer calibration guidelines referenced in SB-1023.

Timing verification
- Use the timing capture device to record multiple cycles through the quench initiation event. Record start and stop markers as defined in SOP-P2-L3-05. If the measured delay exceeds the quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds on any recorded cycle, follow the corrective actions in the acceptance criteria section.

Actuator and lubrication check
- Inspect mechanical actuators for free movement, end play, and visible wear. Clean contact surfaces and apply lubricant CFW-LUB-373 to specified points. The use of any other lubricant is not permitted during calibration checks. After lubrication, cycle the actuator and verify motion is smooth and repeatable. Record any deviation from expected smooth movement and note whether additional mechanical repair is required.

Examples and step rationale
- Example observation: if timing capture shows consistent delay values close to the quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds but not exceeding it, document the trend and schedule follow up inspection. Rationale: trending near limits indicates wear or drift that may progress into nonconformance.  
- Example observation: if a sensor shows a drifting output during hold-to-quench transition, replacing or recalibrating the sensor will reduce variability. Rationale: sensors with degraded response directly affect control timing and thus quench performance.

Records to keep
- Timing capture files annotated with cycle identifiers and operator initials.  
- Completed calibration checklist that includes sensor inspection notes, actuator condition, lubricant application confirmation showing CFW-LUB-373.  
- Any deviation reports and corrective action documentation linked to the furnace work order.  
- Reference to supporting documentation and criteria used during verification, namely SB-1023, SB-1039, and SOP-P2-L3-05.

Acceptance criteria
- Timing and functional: All recorded cycles must show quench initiation delay at or below the quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds. Any cycle exceeding this value requires immediate investigation, corrective action, and re-test before returning to production.  
- Sensor and signal quality: Sensors must provide stable and repeatable signals during the full hold-to-quench transition. Any sensor that fails bench comparison per SB-1023 must be replaced or recalibrated.  
- Mechanical and lubrication: Actuators and moving components must operate smoothly after application of CFW-LUB-373 and must not show binding, excessive play, or evidence of imminent failure. If mechanical defects are observed, document and escalate per SB-1039.

Disposition and follow up
If all acceptance criteria are met, complete the calibration checklist and attach timing capture files and lubricant confirmation to the equipment maintenance record. If any acceptance criterion is not met, implement corrective actions, document the root cause analysis, and repeat verification steps until acceptance is achieved. Reference SOP-P2-L3-05 for any procedure deviations and SB-1023 and SB-1039 for calibration and safety compliance requirements.
